preamble: L-vocalization replaces a lateral, usually the velarized 'dark' [ɫ], with the labio-velar glide [w], keeping the back-of-tongue raising and lip rounding while losing lateral contact. It went to completion in Polish and Sorbian, where almost all historical /ɫ/ became /w/ in every position; in Ukrainian and Belarusian it affected syllable codas; most Brazilian Portuguese dialects vocalize coda /l/; and in Cockney and Estuary English final and preconsonantal /l/ is commonly [w], [o] or [ʊ].

examples.note: Almost all historical /ɫ/ (spelled ł) became /w/, even word-initially and between vowels; the same happened in Sorbian.
Coda /ɫ/ became [w], written ⟨в⟩; Belarusian shows the same change in воўк [vowk], written ⟨ў⟩.
Coda /l/ is vocalized to a back glide in most Brazilian dialects, while European Portuguese keeps a velarized [ɫ].
Final or preconsonantal /l/ is realized as [w], [o] or [ʊ]; the vocalization merges these three words.

sources: Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511611759
